title: Pathfinder (PBHC) Q2 Profit Drops
summary:
Pathfinder Bancorp (NASDAQ:PBHC), a community banking company headquartered in Central New York, released its second quarter earnings on July 30, 2025, for the period ending June 30, 2025. The most significant news was a major credit risk clean-up, including the sale of $9.3 million in nonperforming loans. This resulted in a pre-tax loss of $3.1 million and the sharpest decline in net income in recent periods. There were no analyst estimates available for comparison. Diluted earnings per share (GAAP) came in at less than $0.01, compared to $0.47 last quarter and $0.32 a year ago. Revenue (non-GAAP) was $12.277 million. Overall, the quarter was marked by decisive risk management moves. These actions raised short-term costs but also improved the company's underlying asset quality and efficiency results.

Pathfinder Bancorp is a regional community bank with a strong presence in Oswego County, New York, holding nearly half the county's deposit share. It operates 11 full-service branches and one motor bank, focusing on personal banking, business services, and municipal clients. The company’s primary business is lending to individuals, businesses, and local governments, focusing on commercial real estate and municipal loans.

Recently, it has concentrated on expanding commercial loan products, aiming to increase higher-yielding commercial banking activity while growing a base of stable, low-cost deposits. Strategic initiatives also include improving operational efficiency, managing credit risk, and adapting to regulatory changes such as new loan loss accounting standards. These factors -- loan quality, efficient funding, and regulatory compliance -- are central to the company’s ongoing success.

title: American Water Works (AWK) Q2 Up 11%
summary:
American Water Works (NYSE:AWK), the largest publicly traded U.S. water and wastewater utility, reported results for Q2 2025 on July 30, 2025. The company delivered an 11.1% increase in GAAP revenue to $1,276 million compared to Q2 2024, comfortably above analyst GAAP revenue estimates of $1,217.25 million. However, GAAP earnings per share came in at $1.48, missing the anticipated $1.52. This result was shaped by strong regulated revenue growth and higher capital investment, offset by a notable rise in operating and interest costs. Overall, the quarter underscored American Water Works's continued focus on acquisition-driven expansion and infrastructure renewal, while highlighting the importance of regulatory approvals and cost management.

Source: Analyst estimates for the quarter provided by FactSet.

American Water Works is a regulated utility serving more than 14 million people across 14 states. Its primary mission is to provide clean water and reliable wastewater services through a network of regulated utilities, which together generated 92% of operating revenue for the year ended December 31, 2024.

title: Albemarle (ALB) Q2 Revenue Jumps
summary:
Albemarle (NYSE:ALB), a leading producer of lithium and specialty chemicals, released its second quarter 2025 earnings on July 30, 2025. The headline: Albemarle outperformed analyst estimates on both GAAP revenue and non-GAAP EPS, even as persistent weakness in lithium prices pressured its key Energy Storage segment. Non-GAAP earnings per share were $0.11, well above the $(0.84) forecast, while GAAP revenue reached $1,330.0 million, beating the consensus estimate of $1,222.6 million. However, Both net sales and adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP) declined compared to the prior-year period. The results show the effects of strong volumes, improved productivity, and tight cost control, against ongoing market headwinds.

Source: Analyst estimates provided by FactSet. Management expectations based on management's guidance, as provided in Q1 2025 earnings report.

Albemarle is a global leader in lithium production, supplying compounds essential for lithium-ion batteries powering electric vehicles (EVs) and renewable energy storage. Its business includes three core segments: Energy Storage (mainly lithium), Specialties (bromine and customized lithium solutions), and Ketjen (catalysts and refining chemicals).

title: Graham (GHC) Q2 Revenue Rises 3%
summary:
Graham (NYSE:GHC), a diversified conglomerate with major interests in education, media, healthcare, and manufacturing, reported results on July 30, 2025. The company delivered earnings per share (EPS) of $14.33 (Non-GAAP), well above the analyst estimate of $10.15 (non-GAAP). Revenue (GAAP) reached $1,215.8 million, easily beating GAAP expectations of $1,175.3 million. These results signal a solid operational quarter, marked by improved contributions from education and healthcare, offsetting softness in television broadcasting and automotive businesses.

Source: Analyst estimates for the quarter provided by FactSet.

Graham is a holding company active in education, broadcasting, healthcare, manufacturing, and automotive retail. Its education business, Kaplan, stands out as a global provider of test prep, online, and higher education services. Graham Media Group operates multiple TV stations, while the company’s healthcare arm delivers home health and pharmacy services across several states. Manufacturing and auto segments round out the company’s diverse portfolio, including specialty wood products and car dealerships.
